acceptance_criteria: Typed representations preserve every specified field, array, nullable value and fill alternative under data-pipeline/0.3.
obligations.statement: The solve input represents {events:[{group:string,time:int,value:int|null}],start:int,end:int,width:positive int,fill:'none'|'previous'}. Its result represents an array of {group:string,start:int,count:nonnegative int,value:int|null}. Integers are unbounded mathematical integers and strings are sequences of Unicode scalar values.

acceptance_criteria: The invocation satisfies the declared input structure, width > 0 and start <= end, without additional restrictions on event multiplicity, integer magnitudes, times, values or Unicode strings.
obligations.statement: The caller supplies the specified typed input with width > 0 and start <= end; fill is either none or previous. There are no further input bounds or preconditions.

acceptance_criteria: The canonical source has exactly one admitted entry named solve with arity 1 and the requested typed interface and serialization profile.
For every allowed input, execution produces exactly the finite array specified by O2 through O6; examples alone do not establish universal refinement.
For this guarantee the actual solve source satisfies typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

obligations.statement: Deliver canonical program.vscore.json containing exactly one admitted typed entry solve of arity 1 under vscore/0.3, normative Lean vscore-semantics/0.3 and data-pipeline/0.3. For every input satisfying A1, its actual execution returns the complete grouped bucket aggregation defined by O2 through O6, preserving the specified typed input/output structure. This source implements that function universally and is typed-total, deterministic, input-preserving, without external I/O or floating point, pure data and restricted-runtime-only.

acceptance_criteria: The group sequence equals scalar-codepoint-lexicographic sort of the set of all event group names.
No group is added, duplicated or omitted because its events are out of range.
The actual specified solve source universally implements this formula with all seven required source properties.
obligations.statement: For every allowed input, the group sequence used by solve is exactly the distinct group names from all input events, sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar codepoints, including names whose events are all outside [start,end). The implementation of this formula is the arity-1 solve entry in canonical program.vscore.json and satisfies typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

acceptance_criteria: Each group has exactly one row for every natural k satisfying start+k*width<end and no other bucket starts.
Intervals are left-inclusive and right-exclusive, with the final interval clipped at end.
The actual specified solve source implements the formula universally with all seven source properties and exact unbounded integer arithmetic.

source_refs.interpretation: Strict upper bound and half-open clipped intervals

obligations.statement: For every allowed input and every selected group, bucket starts are exactly b_k=start+k*width for natural k with b_k<end, in increasing k order. Bucket k covers [b_k,min(b_k+width,end)). No buckets exist when start=end. The arity-1 solve in canonical program.vscore.json universally implements this formula with typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

acceptance_criteria: count is exactly the number of qualifying non-null occurrences and sum is their exact integer sum.
Repeated identical events are counted and summed with their full multiplicity.
A bucket with only null values has count zero.
The actual specified solve source universally implements both formulas with all seven required source properties.
obligations.statement: For every allowed input, group g and bucket k, let M(g,k) be the multiset of input event occurrences with group=g, b_k<=time<min(b_k+width,end) and value non-null. The row count equals |M(g,k)| and its bucket sum equals the mathematical sum of their integer values. Null and out-of-range events contribute neither count nor sum; duplicate occurrences contribute separately. The arity-1 solve in canonical program.vscore.json universally implements these formulas with typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

acceptance_criteria: Nonempty buckets return their sum in either fill mode.
Empty buckets follow exactly the none and previous branches, including null before the first nonempty bucket.
Empty buckets do not reset the remembered sum; zero is remembered as a value; prior groups and pre-start events cannot seed it.
The actual specified solve source universally implements the complete causal filling formula with all seven required source properties.

source_refs.interpretation: Zero sum remains a previous value

obligations.statement: For every allowed input and row (g,k), if count(g,k)>0 then value(g,k)=sum(g,k). If count(g,k)=0 and fill=none then value(g,k)=null. If count(g,k)=0 and fill=previous, let j be the greatest index less than k with count(g,j)>0: value(g,k)=sum(g,j) if such j exists, otherwise null. Previous state is group-local, initially null, updated by every nonempty bucket including a zero sum, unchanged by empty buckets, and never seeded by events before start. The arity-1 solve in canonical program.vscore.json universally implements these formulas with typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

acceptance_criteria: Rows are in Unicode scalar lexicographic group order, then increasing bucket start order.
Every row has the specified group, start, count and nullable integer value.
Empty event arrays and start=end produce empty output arrays.
The actual specified solve source implements the complete output formula universally with all seven required source properties.
obligations.statement: For every allowed input, solve returns exactly the concatenation, over the O2 group sequence, of the O3 bucket sequence for that group, with each row {group:g,start:b_k,count:count(g,k),value:value(g,k)} as defined by O4 and O5. There are no extra or omitted rows or fields. The arity-1 solve in canonical program.vscore.json preserves this typed structure and exact order under data-pipeline/0.3 and universally implements the formula with typed_total, deterministic, input_preserved, no_external_io, no_floating_point, pure_data and restricted_runtime_only.

Universal implementation refinement covers all allowed inputs rather than only these examples.
The actual specified solve source satisfies all seven required source properties for this guarantee.
